findings.claim: CoBiT evaluates RAG scientific-claim verification using 707 minimally perturbed claim-counterclaim pairs and measures bias separately at reranking and generation stages. Its experiments find stance-aligned confirmation bias can arise at different stages and can be amplified downstream; evaluated systems also differed in consistency across each pair.
findings.support_locator: ACL Anthology proceedings abstract (n309-op-06); full paper pp. 0-1, especially lines 17-40, 84-123 and 124-175 (n309-op-07). The paper reports these as findings on OpenScholar, ScholarQA, SciRAG and LLM baselines.
findings.decision_implication: Extend the seed's paired-work-product discriminator by asking a scout to search a concise counterclaim with minimally changed stance wording, and compare both the evidence surfaced and the resulting summaries. Where workflow permits, record source discovery/selection separately from the final synthesis; a balanced-looking final answer alone cannot show that contrary evidence was found. Keep expert review of the decisive design choice and direct inspection of cited sources.
findings.assumptions: A meaningful candidate counterclaim can be stated from repository evidence, and the investigator can keep most query/context details fixed while changing the hypothesized direction. For open software design questions, a pair of alternatives may be more appropriate than a strict binary claim pair.
findings.applicability_gap: CoBiT addresses scientific claim verification with stance-flipped factual claims and evaluates particular literature RAG systems. It does not test repository architecture research, Luna-high scouts, mixed-model review, source prompt-injection boundaries, or patch acceptance. Its result motivates an evaluation discriminator; it does not show this workflow change improves the target task.
findings.next_discriminator: On matched repository questions, compare the existing concise-report workflow against one that requires a stance-swapped counterclaim search. Blind-score whether each arm finds relevant contrary evidence and viable alternatives, whether claims are source-supported, and expert correction/time. If retrieval-stage traces are unavailable, report that limitation and score observed source coverage separately from report stance.
findings.incremental_vs_seed: Adds a directly usable counterclaim-pair test and a distinction between evidence selection and final synthesis. This extends seed finding repo-grounding and its matched-investigation falsifier; it narrows the unresolved transfer question by identifying confirmation bias as a concrete failure mode that ordinary source-backed pro/con reporting may not detect. It does not replace the seed's bounded branching, repository-context, prompt-evaluation, or self-critique caveats.

rejected_or_redundant: ReAct was found in search but not used: direct OpenReview PDF access redirected to a browser challenge at n309-op-05, so paper text and publication details were not independently verified in this run.

Evaluation of Attribution Bias (ACL Findings 2025) was opened and verified at n309-op-03 and n309-op-04. Its counterfactual results show authorship metadata can affect attribution for three LLMs, but this was less directly useful than CoBiT's paired-stance, stage-specific test for the present workflow; retained in sources as considered evidence, not a top finding.
Seed access failures retained: two OpenReview PDF attempts hit a browser challenge; one ACL Anthology article returned a cache miss. The seed did not use those papers as evidence.
unresolved: No retrieved study directly tests Luna-high scouting of unfamiliar repositories followed by mixed-model architecture review; effect and transfer remain unknown.

CoBiT's confirmation-bias mechanism and benchmark are scientific-domain, stance-paired evidence. Whether analogous counterclaim searches reveal missed alternatives in real software architecture investigations remains an empirical question.

Prompt-injection boundaries, direct expert access to decisive sources, independent patch acceptance, and timely consequential review remain task requirements; none of the reviewed evidence validates those governance controls.
The seed prompt comparison has not been run; a matched-task expert rubric remains the cheapest target-workflow falsifier.
retained_seed_summary: Seed evidence supports a bounded branching prompt (Tree of Thoughts on constrained tasks), repository artifact/tool grounding (CodeAgent and RepoCod abstracts), metric-based prompt evaluation (MIPRO abstract), and treating critique as a question generator rather than independent verification (RCI abstract). Applicability to open architecture decisions and current mixed-model agents is untested. The seed recommends matched existing-repository tasks scored for viable alternatives, source correctness, omissions and reviewer time; preserve direct expert review, prompt-injection boundaries, and independent patch acceptance. Seed sources retain their original access limits: ToT full text, CodeAgent PDF/opening excerpt, RepoCod and MIPRO abstracts, RCI abstract. Seed also records blocked OpenReview debate/OPRO PDFs and an ACL cache miss; those sources were not treated as evidence.
stop_reason: Stopped after finding one incremental, decision-useful mechanism and discriminator. Used 7 logical web operations total: 2 search queries and 5 opens (including one failed open); within limits of 16 operations, 8 searches and 10 opens. No further search was needed for this bounded addition; elapsed research window was under 12 minutes.
escalation_ready: The seed already supports trying a bounded alternatives prompt with matched-task evaluation. CoBiT adds a concrete falsifier for one-sided evidence handling: stance-swapped counterclaim searches and, when observable, separate assessment of evidence selection from synthesis. Recommend retaining this as a testable workflow variant only; the paper does not support claims about Luna quality gains, architecture decision accuracy, delegation policy, or acceptance controls.
